mechanism: Both drugs can prolong QT interval and cause electrolyte abnormalities (hypokalemia, hypocalcemia), increasing risk of cardiac arrhythmias; foscarnet causes mineral wasting and erythromycin has inherent QT-prolonging properties.
action: Monitor ECG and electrolytes (calcium, magnesium, potassium) regularly; consider alternative antimicrobial if possible; correct electrolyte abnormalities promptly and avoid other QT-prolonging agents.
